scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure: Scheme for Development of Green Estate
description:
The Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance environmental sustainability and promote green spaces across urban and rural areas.

This scheme was officially launched in 2018 as part of the broader efforts to address environmental challenges and improve the quality of life for citizens.

The primary objective of this scheme is to develop green estates and enhance common environmental infrastructure in various regions of India.

The scheme aims to create and maintain parks gardens and other green spaces that contribute to the ecological balance and improve urban aesthetics.

One of the measurable targets of this initiative is to establish at least 100 new green estates by the year 2025.

The scheme also aims to increase the green cover in urban areas by at least 10 percent over the next five years.

Benefits under this scheme include financial assistance for the development of green spaces which can cover up to 70 percent of the total project cost.

The maximum financial assistance provided under this scheme is capped at ₹5 crore per project.

This financial assistance is aimed at local bodies non-governmental organizations and community-based organizations involved in environmental conservation.

Eligibility for this scheme includes local urban bodies such as municipal corporations and municipalities.

Non-governmental organizations that are registered under the Societies Registration Act of 1860 or the Companies Act of 2013 can also apply for assistance.

Community-based organizations that have a proven track record in environmental conservation are eligible to apply.

There are no specific age limits for applicants but organizations must demonstrate their capacity to manage and execute environmental projects.

The application process involves several steps beginning with the submission of a detailed project proposal.

The project proposal must outline the objectives methodology and expected outcomes of the proposed green estate development.

Required documents include proof of registration for NGOs and community organizations along with a detailed budget estimate.

The project proposal must also include a timeline for implementation and maintenance of the green estate.

Once the proposal is submitted it is reviewed by the Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change.

The Ministry may request additional information or clarifications before making a decision on the funding.

Successful applicants will receive a letter of sanction detailing the amount of financial assistance approved.

Disbursement of funds occurs in phases based on the completion of project milestones.

The first installment is typically released upon approval of the project and submission of necessary documentation.

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project as verified by the Ministry.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of community participation in the development and maintenance of green estates.

Regular monitoring and evaluation are conducted to assess the impact of the projects funded under this scheme.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change.

The Ministry has designated specific officers to oversee the implementation and provide guidance to applicants.

Contact details for inquiries can be found on the official website of the Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change.

The scheme encourages innovative approaches to green space development including the use of native plant species and sustainable landscaping practices.

It also promotes the integration of green infrastructure with urban planning to enhance the resilience of cities against climate change.

Statistics indicate that urban areas in India have seen a significant decline in green cover with many cities losing up to 30 percent of their green spaces in the last decade.

The scheme addresses this urgent need for urban greening by providing financial support and technical assistance.

In addition to creating green spaces the scheme also aims to promote biodiversity conservation and improve air quality in urban areas.

The initiative is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals particularly Goal 11 which aims to make cities inclusive safe resilient and sustainable.

The scheme also supports educational initiatives to raise awareness about the importance of green spaces and environmental conservation.

Workshops and training sessions are organized for local bodies and NGOs to enhance their capacity to implement green projects effectively.

The scheme encourages partnerships with educational institutions for research and development in the field of environmental sustainability.

It also provides a platform for sharing best practices and success stories from various projects funded under the scheme.

The overall impact of the scheme is expected to contribute significantly to the improvement of urban ecosystems and the quality of life for residents.

The scheme is part of a larger national strategy to combat climate change and promote sustainable development across India.

As of October 2023 the government has reported the successful establishment of over 50 green estates under this scheme.

These projects have collectively contributed to an increase in green cover by approximately 5 percent in the targeted urban areas.

The scheme has also facilitated the creation of over 2000 jobs in the environmental sector through project implementation and maintenance activities.

Furthermore it has fostered community engagement with thousands of volunteers participating in tree planting and maintenance activities.

The scheme is continuously evolving with feedback from stakeholders being incorporated to enhance its effectiveness.

Future plans include expanding the scope of the scheme to include more comprehensive environmental education programs.

The government is also exploring collaborations with international organizations to bring in global best practices in green infrastructure development.

Through these efforts the Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure aims to create a sustainable and greener future for India.
